scope: React / React DOM documentation. Framework-provided features are not counted as React core.

ssr.note: react-dom/server renders initial HTML with string or stream APIs.

streaming.note: renderToPipeableStream and renderToReadableStream progressively produce HTML.

suspense.note: Suspense displays a fallback until its supported async dependencies resolve; framework integration governs data loading.

client.note: hydrateRoot attaches React behavior to existing server-rendered HTML.
client.label: hydrateRoot

ssg.note: The recommended full-stack frameworks supply static-site generation; it is not a site-export workflow in React core.
ssg.label: App framework

csr.note: createRoot renders and updates browser application UI.

serverOnly.note: Server Components require a supporting framework/bundler. React alone does not supply production routing or deployment.
serverOnly.label: Framework required

partialRendering.note: A prebuilt shell with request-time UI needs an application rendering pipeline.

routing.note: React recommends an application framework, such as React Router or Next.js, for integrated routing.
routing.label: App framework

layouts.note: React core renders UI; template includes/layout composition are available; automatic route-layout selection belongs to the host. React recommends selecting a router or application framework.

dynamicRoutes.note: React core renders UI; route parameter matching belongs to the host router; templates receive prepared values. React recommends selecting a router or application framework.

parallelRoutes.note: React core renders UI; independently navigable routed regions require a host router and client runtime. React recommends selecting a router or application framework.

interceptedRoutes.note: React core renders UI; routed-modal/direct-link behavior belongs to the host router. React recommends selecting a router or application framework.

prefetch.note: React Router Link prefetch can load route data/modules on intent (hover/focus), render or viewport entry. It requires a configured router/framework mode; React core alone does not prefetch navigation destinations.
prefetch.label: React Router

softNavigation.note: React Router Link/useNavigate and router providers support browser history and navigation without document reloads. React core alone does not provide a router.
softNavigation.label: React Router

viewTransitions.note: React Router integrates animated navigation with browser View Transitions. Current v8 docs deprecate the Link viewTransition option in favor of React ViewTransition; choose a compatible React/router version. Styling and reduced-motion handling remain application-owned.
viewTransitions.label: React Router

redirects.note: React core renders UI; HTTP redirects and URL rewrites are owned by the host server/router. React recommends selecting a router or application framework.

serverData.note: Server Components can load data before client delivery; build/transport/cache integration requires a supporting framework.
serverData.label: Server Components / framework

clientData.note: The guide recommends purpose-built data libraries including TanStack Query and SWR for browser request state/caching.
clientData.label: TanStack Query / SWR

requestDedupe.note: cache memoizes equivalent calls within a Server Components request; it is not a general client cache or persistent data cache.
requestDedupe.label: RSC cache

persistentCache.note: Retaining application data or rendered pages across requests belongs to the host cache.

invalidation.note: Application data/page invalidation belongs to the host; recompiling a template is a different cache boundary.

isr.note: Regenerating deployed pages requires a host page cache/export pipeline.

apiRoutes.note: The host server exposes HTTP endpoints and invokes the template renderer.

httpErrors.note: The reviewed renderer does not own the HTTP response. The host server must select 404/5xx, map routing/render failures, and decide when headers are committed. Displaying an error or fallback in rendered HTML does not establish the HTTP status.
httpErrors.label: HTTP host required

actions.note: Next.js App Router is one implementation of React Server Functions; a hosting framework is needed for the end-to-end server transport.
actions.label: App framework

forms.note: Function-valued form actions integrate pending state, optimistic UI, and error handling. Server-function transport requires a supporting framework.
forms.label: Form actions

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Function-valued form actions integrate pending state, optimistic UI, and error handling. Server-function transport requires a supporting framework.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Request middleware belongs to the host server.

cookies.note: HTTP cookies and sessions belong to the host request/response layer.

cssModules.note: React delegates styling builds to tools such as Vite/Parcel; CSS Modules support comes from that selected tool.
cssModules.label: Build tool

scopedCss.note: className and inline style do not compile scoped selectors; use a stylesheet build tool or styling library.

tailwind.note: React accepts authored className values; Tailwind’s scanner/compiler is separate application tooling.

cssInJs.note: React can render/deduplicate style elements; a CSS-in-JS language/compiler must be supplied by a styling library.

images.note: Templates emit image markup; image resizing/conversion requires a separate asset pipeline.

fonts.note: Font downloading, subsetting, and fallback optimization require a separate asset pipeline.

scripts.note: Async script elements are hoisted and deduplicated; React also exposes preinit/preload resource hints. This is not an all-purpose third-party consent scheduler.

assetPipeline.note: React and React DOM render UI; they do not own an asset build or deployment pipeline. A framework or separately configured build tool must fingerprint files, update references, and set delivery cache headers.
assetPipeline.label: Build tool required

staticAssets.note: Serving files and assigning cache headers belong to the host web server.

metadata.note: React hoists title elements into the document head. Multiple simultaneous titles are not automatically merged; the application must ensure one.
metadata.label: Element-level support

assessment.label: Element-level support
assessment.summary: Head element hoisting is useful, but it does not by itself establish a route-aware metadata system.
strengths: A rendered title element can use component values and move into the document head.
tradeoffs: The application must ensure only one title is rendered; multiple titles are not automatically resolved.
Routing, inherited metadata policy, and generated SEO assets depend on the surrounding application/framework.

dynamicMetadata.note: Title text can come from component values; this does not establish layout metadata inheritance.

metadataInheritance.note: Template inheritance/content composition is separate from a metadata-field inheritance contract.

metadataOverrides.note: A host head component or template block can override markup; structured field merge/clear rules are application-owned.

titleTemplates.note: Titles can use template expressions; ancestor metadata/title-template policy belongs to the application.

socialImages.note: Generating social-preview image bytes needs a separate image renderer/service.

sitemaps.note: XML can be templated, but route enumeration and a sitemap generator belong to the host.

robots.note: Text can be templated, but crawler-document publishing/configuration belongs to the host.

markdown.note: This is text/HTML templating; Markdown parsing and content-page integration require another tool.

collections.note: The host loads and validates structured content; the template API renders supplied values.

draftMode.note: Editorial preview authorization and published-cache bypass belong to the host application.

translations.note: react-i18next provides message translation, pluralization, and interpolation.
translations.label: react-i18next

localeRouting.note: Language URL matching/detection belongs to the host router.

localeFormatting.note: Locale-aware number/date formatting belongs to Intl or an i18n library; it is not supplied by React’s rendering API.

auth.note: Identity, login, and authorization are responsibilities of the host application.

csp.note: The stream renderer accepts nonce for generated scripts. The host must generate nonces and set the matching HTTP policy.
csp.label: Stream nonce option

cspNonce.note: The stream renderer accepts nonce for generated scripts. The host must generate nonces and set the matching HTTP policy.
cspNonce.label: Stream nonce option

csrf.note: HTML escaping does not establish CSRF protection; the host must protect mutation endpoints.

environment.note: Server/client secret configuration belongs to the host application, not template evaluation.

types.note: The official guide uses TypeScript with @types/react and @types/react-dom; those type packages are maintained through DefinitelyTyped.
types.label: TypeScript / DefinitelyTyped

hmr.note: Vite, Parcel, and Rsbuild integrate Fast Refresh during development; React alone is not a dev server.
hmr.label: Bundler Fast Refresh

cli.note: This renderer integrates with its language/build toolchain rather than supplying an application CLI.

bundleAnalysis.note: Production browser/server bundle inspection belongs to the host build toolchain.

unitTests.note: React Testing Library supplies DOM-oriented component testing utilities; install an external test runner and DOM environment as appropriate.
unitTests.label: React Testing Library

e2eTests.note: Browser end-to-end setup belongs to the chosen application framework/test runner, not React core.

observability.note: Profiler reports component render timing through a callback. Profiling has overhead and is disabled in ordinary production builds; production profiling requires the special profiling build. Server request traces/metrics remain host-owned.
observability.label: Profiler / profiling build

errorHandling.note: Error boundary components use getDerivedStateFromError/componentDidCatch for descendant UI failures. They do not catch every event, async callback, or server-rendering failure.

serverHosting.note: The renderer needs a host server; it is not a production server runtime.

subpathProxy.note: The reviewed UI library does not own production HTTP routing, asset mounting or reverse-proxy origin handling. A router/build tool and host framework must coordinate a subpath deployment; client-side route base support alone is not the complete server deployment contract.
subpathProxy.label: Host framework required

staticHosting.note: Publishing generated pages requires a host export/deployment workflow.

containers.note: A container packages the host application and renderer together; the template API has no container workflow.

edgeHosting.note: Edge deployment depends on the host runtime and its adapter, not template syntax.

orm.note: ORM / query builder belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

migrations.note: Schema migrations belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

transactions.note: Transactions belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

jobs.note: Background jobs belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

mail.note: Email belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

uploads.note: File uploads & storage belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

realtime.note: Real-time delivery belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

xssEscaping.note: Normal text values are rendered as text; dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses this path and requires trusted/sanitized HTML. Do not infer arbitrary URL/CSS safety from text escaping.

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

authorization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific authorization policies contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

rateLimiting.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific rate limiting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: React Router framework-mode Form produces a real server submission before JavaScript loads and enhances it afterward. A plain client-only React app has no server action endpoint from React core.
progressiveEnhancement.label: React Router framework mode

optimisticUi.note: React useOptimistic overlays pending mutation UI and reconciles against the supplied confirmed state through Actions/transitions. Application code must define the update and failure feedback; this is not a durable offline write queue.
optimisticUi.label: React useOptimistic

requestCancellation.note: React Router cancels interrupted navigations/fetcher requests and discards stale revalidation responses. The server may still process canceled requests; this is not backend rollback.
requestCancellation.label: React Router

typedLinks.note: React Router framework type generation and href utilities check registered paths and required route parameters. Framework-mode type generation must run; this is not a React core router.
typedLinks.label: React Router type generation

searchParams.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific validated url state contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

stateRestoration.note: Nested router layouts can preserve mounted parent UI while outlets change. Unmounted route component state is not automatically retained; arbitrary form drafts need URL/session/app storage.
stateRestoration.label: React Router layouts

scrollRestoration.note: ScrollRestoration emulates browser restoration after data loads, with custom keys and reset controls. It requires a data/framework router and does not establish automatic nested-scrollport restoration.
scrollRestoration.label: React Router

navigationBlocking.note: useBlocker can pause SPA navigation and let the application proceed/reset after an unsaved-change prompt. Hard reloads and cross-origin navigation require separate browser handling.
navigationBlocking.label: React Router

navigationAccessibility.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessible navigation contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

a11yChecks.note: The recommended eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y integration statically checks JSX accessibility patterns. This is an external lint tool, not runtime enforcement or accessibility certification.
a11yChecks.label: eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y

lazyActivation.note: The linked rendering API review does not establish the specific deferred activation contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

codeSplitting.note: Framework mode splits browser route modules and removes server-only exports. Declarative router usage alone does not enable this build pipeline.
codeSplitting.label: React Router framework mode

offline.note: The linked deployment API review does not establish the specific offline integration contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

scheduling.note: Scheduled tasks requires a host application or specialized integration beyond the reviewed UI API. Emitting markup or using arbitrary host-language libraries does not establish this application-level contract.

notifications.note: Multi-channel notifications requires a host application or specialized integration beyond the reviewed UI API. Emitting markup or using arbitrary host-language libraries does not establish this application-level contract.

searchIndex.note: Search indexing requires a host application or specialized integration beyond the reviewed UI API. Emitting markup or using arbitrary host-language libraries does not establish this application-level contract.

fieldEncryption.note: Encrypted model fields requires a host application or specialized integration beyond the reviewed UI API. Emitting markup or using arbitrary host-language libraries does not establish this application-level contract.

httpTests.note: The linked testing API review does not establish the specific http integration tests contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.
